body:
I restarted Godot and the issue went away (4.4.1-stable was freshly started just to test it). Seems like it builds up over time.

I found people taking about macOS 26 having bugs in input drivers on WoW forums: https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/new-mac-specific-performance-issue-affecting-macos-26/2167645.

Possibly a macOS 26-specific issue, though other apps (e.g. Chrome, Rider, Notes) work well even when running for hours.

@robsontenorio Yes, the WoW forums post I linked has a workaround (https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/new-mac-specific-performance-issue-affecting-macos-26/2167645/31):

> Open terminal and run this command to disable autofill heuristic controller
> `defaults write -g NSAutoFillHeuristicControllerEnabled -bool FALSE`

(You might need to restart Godot after running this)

The same workaround was suggested in other places, and some apps even decide to set `NSAutoFillHeuristicControllerEnabled` to `false` on startup just to avoid this issue, so it should be somewhat safe.

In my case, with this workaround, everything has been running fine for past 3 weeks.

Unfortunately it didn't work for me, even restarting Godot.

But , at some point this fix should be included  in Godot , right ?

> Unfortunately it didn't work for me, even restarting Godot.

From what I've read online new macOS seems to be pretty buggy to some users. For me it's fine now, so I can't really debug it and see what's wrong, and whether the issue is in Godot or maybe some system driver.

Since `NSAutoFillHeuristicControllerEnabled` fix doesn't work for you, you might have a completely different issue that was not either discovered before or has no known workaround right now.

> But , at some point this fix should be included in Godot , right ?

Difficult to say, the issue that `NSAutoFillHeuristicControllerEnabled` fixes is a system driver issue, and the workaround is not perfect - it might temporarily break some Apple Intelligence features, so I don't know if including it directly in Godot is the best option. It's really Apple who should step up and just fix their buggy drivers.

For future reference, the issue was with Swish (similar to Rectangle and other window managers). 

Once it was turned off, everything became smooth again in Godot. 

I have notified the developers. 

https://highlyopinionated.co/swish

@robsontenorio You're a lifesaver. I would have never figure it out myself

I'd like to throw my two cents in on this issue. I don't use Swish or any window managers.  I've concluded that Godot is doing something different with mouse scroll events but I don't exactly know what it is yet. I'm using a Logitech MX Master 4 on macOS. I'm also using Logitech's Logi Options+ software.  I have smooth scrolling turned off in Logi and in Godot. And I have the scrolling speed set to its lowest value. And yet, a single mouse scroll event in Godot causes a 36 line jump in the script editor and a large zoom jump in the 2D scene editor. But in other applications such as BBEdit, scrolling does not behave that way there. BBEdit seems to scroll one line at a time which is what I would expect.  Disabling the Logi software or using a generic USB mouse results in normal scrolling and zooming behaviour in Godot.  So it seems that mouse scroll events coming from Logi Options+ are not being interpreted by Godot in the same way as other macOS applications do.  Magic Trackpad zooming and scrolling events, conversely, are a dream!

Would love to see some additional mouse wheel tweaks put in place to fix this.

I am using Godot v4.8.dev6.official [8898c2b3d] at the time of this writing.

@PrismaticRealms I'm having the same issue using my Logitech MX Anywhere 2 & the Logi Options+ software: The trackpad now behaves in a much nicer way, thanks to the [[trackpad fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111305)] that landed in v4.8.dev6, but I noticed the scrolling on my mouse is really sensitive - basically unusable, which wasn't the case in previous versions. When I uninstall the Logi Options+ software, it works normally.

I wondered if it was being caused by that same fix that I linked to, but the overly sensitive scrolling also occurs version v4.8.dev5, suggesting it must be caused by something else. In version dev4 and earlier, the mouse works as expected.
**EDIT:** Seems like it was caused by this [[commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123072)], but I'm not sure.

Maybe I should open a new issue since this problems seems bit different from the original post.

**EDIT 2:** For anyone that wants a quick fix to this, completely uninstalling Logi Options+ could be an option for you! I noticed I can actually do without it, and the open-source alternative, OpenLogi, even works as a replacement if needed (You need to set the scrolling behavior to "Standard" and not "High Resolution" though, or else the fast scrolling returns).
This should still probably not be happening, though. I also briefly tested BetterMouse, which showed aforementioned scrolling issues, as well.
